Hypertension is another name for high blood pressure. It means the force of your blood pushing against the walls of your arteries stays higher than it should over time. It often has no symptoms, so it's important to measure it regularly. Do you have any other questions about your ACCESS care?

The things most commonly discussed for bringing blood pressure down are everyday ones: less salt, more movement, losing some weight if that applies, limiting alcohol, sleeping well, and taking any prescribed medicine exactly as prescribed.
